headline: Run the planner on Brisk-S with low reasoning and one retry: the cheapest setting to clear the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} pass-rate gate, though by only {weakest.margin|abs} points, inside the noise.
lede: It passes {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} of its cases at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s.low.r1} per thousand calls, but a fresh run of this size would read it below the gate {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.wrong_side} of the time. If the gate must hold on its interval, Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry is the pick, at {cost.gap.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.multiple} the cost.

caveats.material_if: Only if the pick's true pass rate sits below the gate: a fresh run of today's size would read it there {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.wrong_side} of the time, and then Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry becomes the pick.
Only if the pick reads high by luck, being the setting of {n_candidates|words} that lands nearest above the line; a rerun on fresh cases would likely read it lower, toward or under the gate.
Only for the comparison between the two Brisk-S settings, which is read unpaired and so wider than a paired one; the gate reads each setting on its own figure and does not rest on it.

caveats.label: Task mix
caveats.material_if: Only if live traffic carries more multi-hop or ambiguous-entity queries than the eval did: the pick sits below the gate on both, so a heavier share of them would pull its overall rate under the line.

decision.text: Brisk-S, low reasoning, one retry. It is the cheapest of the {count.passing.pass_rate|words} settings that clear the gate, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.low.r1} a month at the declared volume, and the only one no other setting beats on both cost and pass rate.

Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry clears the gate with room, but costs {cost.gap.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.multiple} as much, and its lead of {compare.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.difference|abs} points is not told apart from zero ({compare.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval}). The Atlas-M settings that pass cost {cost.gap.atlas-m.low.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.multiple} as much or more. No Nano-XS setting reaches the gate; its best reads {criteria.pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1.value}.

The weakest margin is the pick's own: {weakest.arm} reads {weakest.value} against the {weakest.threshold} gate, {weakest.margin|abs} points clear, and its computed interval ({spread.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval}) crosses the line. A run that settles it four times in five needs {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.cases_needed_two_sided_80} cases, so more cases are not a practical way out.

The planner owner declares whether the gate must hold on its interval or on its point estimate. On the interval, switch to Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry, which costs {cost.gap.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.monthly|abs} more a month.

claims.text: Only {count.passing.pass_rate|words} of {n_candidates|words} settings clear the gate, and Brisk-S with low reasoning and one retry is the cheapest of them.

evidence.caption: Pass rate against cost per thousand calls for every setting, cost on a log axis; the gate sits at {criteria.pass_rate.threshold}.

claims.text: The pick's clearance is inside the noise: its computed interval ({spread.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval}) crosses the gate, while Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry sits wholly above it ({spread.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval}).

evidence.caption: Pass rate of the settings that clear the gate, each with a computed interval, against the gate line.
How far each Brisk-S setting sits from the gate, how often a fresh run of today's size would read it on the other side, and the cases a settling run needs.

claims.text: Moving up to high reasoning costs {cost.gap.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.monthly|abs} more a month for a pass-rate lift not told apart from zero.

evidence.caption: High-reasoning Brisk-S minus low-reasoning Brisk-S, both with one retry, in pass-rate points; only the overall row carries an interval, unpaired.

claims.text: A retry lifts Brisk-S's pass rate at every reasoning level, by {lever.retry.brisk-s.low.r0.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.effect|abs} points at low reasoning for {cost.gap.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.low.r0.per_1k|abs} more per thousand calls; it is what carries the pick over the gate.

evidence.caption: What each Brisk-S setting buys in pass-rate points when it alone changes, with unpaired intervals; the last rows show whether reasoning's lift differs with a retry.

claims.text: The pick's misses sit in multi-hop and ambiguous-entity queries, where it reads {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean} and {task.disamb.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}; this split is descriptive.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by kind of query for the two Brisk-S settings with one retry; the gate line applies overall, not per kind.
The failed cases kept for the pick, one per kind of query that misses; the snapshot does not say how many failures they were drawn from.

explore.control: How the gate is read: on the point estimate or on the whole interval
explore.outcome: On the point estimate the pick is low reasoning with one retry, at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s.low.r1} per thousand calls. On the interval its range ({spread.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval}) crosses the line, and high reasoning with one retry, at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s.high.r1}, is the cheapest whose range clears it.

explore.binds: The pick, read on point estimates
explore.outcome: The pick holds for any line above Brisk-S low reasoning without a retry ({criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0.value}) up to its own {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.value}. Above that, Brisk-S high reasoning with one retry holds up to {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.value}, then Atlas-M high reasoning with one retry up to {criteria.pass_rate.atlas-m.high.r1.value}; past it no setting passes. Each of these points carries its own interval, so each switch is a band, not a sharp line.

method.text: Each setting ran {scoreboard.brisk-s.low.r1.cases} research queries across four kinds (single lookup, multi-hop, date and unit math, ambiguous entity), with no repeats stated and none lost. Per-kind case counts are not stated.
Each query is graded pass or fail; the campaign does not state the rule that makes a plan pass. Kept failures show a missing call, wrong arguments and a wrong tool.
One gate, declared for the campaign: overall pass rate at least {criteria.pass_rate.threshold}, read here on each setting's point estimate.

The pipeline states no interval on pass rate. Intervals shown are computed here from each setting's binomial spread over its cases, by normal approximation. Comparisons between settings are unpaired, so wider than a paired reading of the same cases; there is no control arm and no correction across comparisons.

Cost per thousand planner calls as measured. Monthly figures multiply it by the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month}, whose unit the input does not state; if it counts tasks rather than calls, monthly costs run higher.
